svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: A self-contained flower anatomy learning interface. Ten lettered slots point to flower structures. Clicking a word-bank tile previews its matching slot and highlights the structure. Only one preview is shown at a time. Hint, Check Answer and Reset open closable panels through internal fragment links and CSS target selectors. This static SVG does not perform physical dragging, retain placements or calculate a score. A pollination inset shows pollen moving from anther to stigma. Open the SVG directly in a browser to use the links; image-only viewers may display just the starting screen.
svg.metadata: Generalized complete flower with a superior ovary, shown partly in longitudinal section. A stamen comprises anther and filament. The depicted pistil comprises stigma, style and ovary. Receptacle means the expanded stem tip to which the floral parts attach, not the whole flower stalk. Concept reference: https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/32-1-reproductive-development-and-structure . Native SVG elements, embedded CSS, internal hyperlinks only. No JavaScript, SMIL, raster data, external stylesheets, external fonts or external rendering resources.

g.text: Explore the structures that help flowering plants reproduce.
A–J identify ten structures. Brackets indicate a whole organ.
Preview only · one label at a time; no saved answers.

g.text: Start outside the flower, then work toward its center.

text.tspan: Petals attract attention. Sepals sit beneath them
and protect the flower while it is a bud.
Find an anther at the tip of a filament.
Together, those two structures form a stamen.
Trace stigma → style → ovary down the pistil.
The receptacle supports the floral parts below.

g.text: Tip: D and H point to brackets around complete organs.
